results.name: Inside an AhsayCBS Intrusion: Hidden Webshells, a CryptoMiner, and a C2 Implant
results.description: Between October 8 and 11, 2026, threat actors exploited authentication bypass and remote code execution vulnerabilities in AhsayCBS backup management software to compromise multiple servers. The intrusion involved deploying five distinct webshell families with varying capabilities, including command execution, file operations, and encrypted payload loaders hidden in PNG images. Attackers installed two XMRig cryptocurrency miners with scheduled task persistence, staged tunneling tools, and deployed a custom Python-based implant with environmental keying that communicated with command-and-control infrastructure. The operators created Microsoft Defender exclusions, accessed backup credentials through Veeam database queries, and specifically targeted backup infrastructure to potentially access stored credentials for hypervisors and domain accounts. The sophisticated multi-stage attack demonstrated significant operational patience beyond typical smash-and-grab cryptomining campaigns.

results.name: Trusted by Default: Qubole Cross-Account Access Abused in the Wild
results.description: A threat actor exploited IAM credentials from Qubole's AWS account (805246085872) to assume integration roles in customer environments between October 14 and October 26, 2026. The attacker used two IAM users and multiple VPN addresses to gain access, then conducted extensive reconnaissance across affected AWS accounts. Activities included enumerating storage, databases, and identity resources, harvesting credentials from Lambda environment variables, Secrets Manager, and SSM Parameter Store, and validating discovered credentials using TruffleHog. The actor exfiltrated data from S3 buckets opportunistically, downloading whatever each assumed role could access. A suspicious bootable Linux ISO image was also identified, designed for remote deployment and system reconnaissance. The campaign appears opportunistic rather than state-sponsored, exploiting trusted cross-account relationships that remained active despite many integrations being unused.

results.name: On the hunt for ARTEX: understanding agentic attacks in AWS environments
results.description: In October 2026, an AI-native penetration framework called ARTEX was observed conducting attacks against AWS environments, primarily targeting financial data. ARTEX operates through LLM agents that autonomously plan and execute attacks based on operator-defined objectives. Observed activity included exploitation of compromised long-term IAM access keys to search CloudWatch logs for financial information, file paths, and secrets. Additionally, attackers abused public Amazon Cognito user pools through anonymous sign-ups, token collection, and AWS account enumeration. Datadog identified hundreds of internet-exposed ARTEX consoles, often in Mandarin and hosted in Singapore and Hong Kong. The framework has been linked to China-aligned threat actor Storm-0940 and demonstrates sophisticated post-exploitation capabilities including automated resource discovery and credential harvesting across cloud environments.

results.name: Infostealer VOLTA That Has AI Assess Stolen Information
results.description: VOLTA is a Windows-based infostealer that incorporates an LLM assessment phase to evaluate stolen data. It operates through multiple phases: stealing credentials, sessions, and cryptocurrency wallets from browsers and applications; enriching data by querying external services with stolen tokens; sending bundled information to LLMs via OpenRouter to assess victim monetization value; and exfiltrating data through Telegram. The malware employs sophisticated techniques including Chrome App-Bound Encryption bypass, BIP-39 seed phrase validation, and automatic model switching when encountering refusals. Only one sample has been observed, submitted to VirusTotal in October 2026, with no confirmed in-the-wild usage.

results.name: Analyzing an Illegal Android Gambling App Built with Flutter
results.description: A Flutter-based Android malware campaign distributes an illegal online gambling application disguised as a Macau casino clone. The malware employs a sophisticated multi-tiered infrastructure with configuration servers, registration servers, and game servers. Victims engage in rigged casino games where mathematical odds favor cybercriminals, while the platform exploits gambling addiction through VIP recharges and referral schemes. The application exfiltrates sensitive data including geolocation coordinates, phone numbers, and device information through encrypted channels using AES encryption and HMAC-SHA256 authentication. Communication flows through multiple server tiers, with fallback mechanisms ensuring persistent connectivity. The malware represents professional-grade development with clean REST APIs and comprehensive backend ecosystem, though improved reverse engineering tools in 2026 have made analysis more feasible compared to 2024.

results.name: Malicious bee-js npm Release and Swarm Desktop Releases Deliver SleepyDuck Ethereum C2 Backdoor
results.description: On November 9, 2026, threat actors compromised Ethersphere's release pipeline through two compromised GitHub accounts, publishing malicious @ethersphere/bee-js 13.3.0 to npm and trojanized Swarm Desktop 0.56.2 releases. Both artifacts contained loaders fetching JavaScript from api[.]frameworkmetrics[.]xyz with full Node.js privileges. The infrastructure, including Ethereum smart contract 0xf8a900Db50b3331be6B768bA460BB59f3E40C344 for C2 addressing, matches SleepyDuck/EtherDuck operations from October 2026 targeting Open VSX extensions. The malicious npm package ran through legitimate trusted publishing workflows with valid SLSA provenance, while Swarm Desktop releases were signed with Apple Developer ID and notarized. Payloads exfiltrated Bee node passwords and wallet keys, then deployed Go backdoors on macOS/Linux and ScreenConnect remote access tools on Windows, specifically targeting developers working with Ethereum tooling.

results.name: Contagious Interview - One Interview Away From Infection
results.description: A sophisticated campaign targeting software developers through fake job interviews has been exposed, using a fraudulent company called AccuraSoftHire as a front. The operation lures developers through legitimate job platforms like Indeed and Glassdoor, with recruiters using identity-verified LinkedIn profiles. Candidates receive take-home coding assignments containing malicious npm packages disguised as Tailwind CSS plugins. When built, these packages deploy loaders that fetch additional payloads from remote servers using blockchain dead drops. The company's career site also serves a fake camera driver that delivers the same malware. This attack vector, linked to previous North Korean campaigns, has infected tens of thousands of machines globally and resulted in significant cryptocurrency theft, including the Binance breach exceeding six billion dollars.

results.name: The Industry Leader in Enterprise Brand Protection
results.description: A sophisticated phishing campaign has been identified targeting hospitality customers through fake hotel reservation pages impersonating Booking.com and other hotel services. The operation uses personalized reservation details including hotel names, dates, prices, guest information, and contact details to enhance credibility. Two main visual templates share the same underlying codebase: one closely mimics Booking.com while another uses generic Best Hotel Reservation branding. The kit employs advanced features including real-time card validation using Luhn checksums, interactive verification workflows, multi-language support spanning Japanese, Chinese, Korean, European languages and others, and three backend endpoints for tracking victim progression. Pages continue interaction after initial card submission through polling mechanisms that can present additional verification prompts. results.name: Shai-Hulud Descendant Surfaces in Malicious Ruby Gem That Steals Credentials and Poisons AI Tools
results.description: A malicious Ruby gem, strutil-core version 1.0.1, executes a 5.48 MB credential-stealing worm during installation. Published on November 1, 2026, by RubyGems account jamnajiea, the package was flagged 70 seconds after release and removed within five hours. The payload, a new build of the testmetest worm from the Miasma family descended from the Shai-Hulud toolkit, steals credentials from cloud services, CI systems, package registries, SSH, AI coding tools, and cryptocurrency wallets. It propagates through RubyGems, npm, PyPI, JFrog Artifactory, GitHub, GitLab, and SSH. The worm installs a Python backdoor controlled via signed GitHub commits, poisons AI tool configurations to maintain persistence, and includes a conditional wiper that deletes the user's home directory when a stolen GitHub token is revoked. The malware targets Linux and macOS systems on x86-64 and ARM64 architectures, excluding Russian-speaking locales.

results.name: ARTEX abuse expands as cybercriminals target financial sector
results.description: In October 2026, the Cambodia-based threat actor Storm-3358 began leveraging the agentic AI offensive framework ARTEX to target financial organizations primarily in Southeast Asia and select global institutions. The group combines ARTEX with conventional automated tools to scan internet-connected systems, exploit vulnerabilities including anonymous file upload and server-side request forgery, and deploy open-source remote access trojans such as WISP, vshell, and AdaptixC2. ARTEX agents perform credential compromise, web shell deployment, lateral movement, privilege escalation, and data exfiltration at machine speed. This activity demonstrates an emerging trend of threat actors accelerating attack chains through agentic AI penetration testing frameworks, requiring defenders to similarly adopt AI-powered detection and response capabilities.
